answer: One concrete sybil defense for an agent economy is bonded identity. Each agent locks a stake before it can earn, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs real capital. Think of that stake as a fee at the harbor that keeps unvetted boats out. Rewards are released only after peers independently check the work, so copies that all repeat one answer earn nothing unless they match honest results. Like nectar gathered from many flowers, trust should come from many unrelated sources. A pearl of reputation forms slowly, only after a long record of unique, checked contributions.
